About.title: about me
About.description: i'm a fourth-semester computer science student at ufpb, focused on artificial intelligence, data and software development. i build pipelines that turn unstructured documents, such as handwritten prescriptions, danfes (brazilian invoice documents) and legislative texts, into structured data, using ocr, vision-language models and natural language processing (nlp), and i develop web applications with react, next.js and java. in my free time, i solve [competitive programming](https://github.com/larissagondim/competitiveProgramming) problems (codeforces, atcoder, beecrowd, codechef) because i enjoy racking my brain over a good challenge. i use linux as my main environment. outside of code, i find balance in drawing, music and nintendo games.

Projects.title: pauta – municipal political participation platform
Projects.shortDescription: a municipal political participation platform: citizens report urban problems with a photo and location, a vision LLM classifies the category and the problem becomes a point on the map; the system also recommends candidates by affinity of political agendas. project stack: next.js, react, typescript, fastapi, python, postgres with postgis and pgvector, supabase and celery.
contributionsAndAchievements: preprocessed 2,103 legislative proposals from 97 city councilors in 5 municipalities of paraíba (sapl data): null handling and separation between interface data and NLP data.
tokenization, stopword removal and lemmatization with SpaCy and NLTK, with custom stopwords for legislative jargon.
plain-language summaries of the 2,103 proposals with llama 3.1 via groq, shown to citizens.
foundation of the recommendation system: councilor embeddings with portuguese BERT and an autoencoder (768 to 64 dimensions) in pytorch, with training and validation notebooks.

Projects.title: pokémon ADT
Projects.shortDescription: a low-level pokémon battle simulation engine developed in c, focusing on strict abstract data type (ADT) concepts and optimized memory management.
contributionsAndAchievements: built a low-level modular architecture that encapsulates pokémon lifecycles, moves, and attributes via strict contracts in .h header files.
modeled and implemented core game algorithms for official damage calculation, status modifiers, and type effectiveness charts.
maintained rigorous control over dynamic memory allocation (malloc/free) to guarantee clean execution and prevent memory leaks.
manipulated strings and pointers directly to emulate a turn-based action execution queue inside the terminal.

Projects.title: pokédex game
Projects.shortDescription: an interactive 3D pokédex with battles, machine-learning win prediction and a tamagotchi, covering all 1,025 pokémon.
contributionsAndAchievements: built a procedural 3D pokédex device with react three fiber, including pressable buttons, sound, gamepad support and a phone layout.
wrote a typescript battle engine from scratch supporting 1v1, 3v3 and 6v6 formats with move, item and switch menus.
trained a machine-learning win predictor that runs in the browser and shows a pre-battle win chance plus a live monte carlo estimate.
developed python scrapers to collect data, sprites and artwork for all 1,025 pokémon, and a tamagotchi mode with needs, xp, evolution and egg hatching.

Projects.title: competitive programming

contributionsAndAchievements: implemented optimal solutions for diverse algorithmic challenges covering arrays, matrices, strings, and mathematical logic.
focused on code efficiency, runtime optimization, and memory constraints required by competitive platforms.
